faq.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.subheading: In-depth answers regarding my background, project execution, technical capabilities, and collaboration scope.

items.question: Were the projects in your portfolio built independently, and what was your exact role?
items.answer: Yes, all projects displayed—including BusinessOS, Lumière Parfums, and Gym CRM—are self-directed products that I conceived, designed, and engineered independently. For each project, I handled the full product scope: defining the operational problem, structuring the user workflows, designing responsive interfaces with Tailwind CSS, writing type-safe TypeScript code, and configuring live deployments on Vercel. For full-stack applications like BusinessOS, this also included relational data modeling with Prisma and PostgreSQL. Live interactive demos and open GitHub repositories are available for each project.

items.question: What technical stack do you work with, and do you handle both frontend and backend development?
items.answer: I work primarily within the modern TypeScript and Next.js ecosystem. On the frontend, I build component-driven, responsive user interfaces using Next.js (App Router), React, and Tailwind CSS, focusing on clean structure and lightweight bundles (such as the 103 kB shared First Load JS on this portfolio). On the backend, I develop relational data models, REST endpoints, and server actions using Prisma ORM with PostgreSQL and SQLite, while integrating Recharts for data visualization and Zod for strict input schema validation.

items.question: How do you approach security, validation, and production quality in your applications?
items.answer: I apply defensive engineering principles tailored to each application's requirements. Across my web projects, I implement strict Zod schema validation, input sanitization, and request rate limiting on sensitive routes. In full-stack platforms like BusinessOS, I implemented Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) and dedicated server-side demo guards (DEMO_MODE) that allow visitors to safely explore administrative views while preventing destructive database mutations. Every project is tested for mobile responsiveness and cross-device consistency.

items.question: How does your background in Business Analytics & AI influence how you build software?
items.answer: Studying Business Analytics & AI at EMAA Business School trains me to evaluate digital tools through the lens of organizational workflows, data structure, and operational decision-making. Before writing code, I analyze how information moves through a process, where operational friction occurs, and how relational data should be structured. This analytical perspective—reinforced by practical exposure to administrative workflows during my internship at the Wilaya de la Région Souss-Massa—guides me to build software focused on real workflow utility and clear operational metrics.

items.question: What kinds of professional opportunities, internships, or collaborations are you open to?
items.answer: As an early-career builder and student, I am open to internship opportunities, junior software development or data analytics roles, technical collaborations with founders, and selected freelance product projects. I am particularly interested in teams and environments where I can apply my analytical thinking, Next.js/TypeScript development skills, and product execution mindset to build reliable digital tools and solve practical operational problems.
